turns.learner: Hello! Can you give me an exercise on he, she and it with -s?
turns.tutor:
Hello! I'll show you one example first.
They sleep late on Saturdays. Tom sleeps late on Saturdays.
I think: Tom is one person, so he is "he". With "he", the verb needs -s: sleeps.
Rule: after he, she or it, add -s or -es to the verb.
Right: She eats fruit every day. Wrong: She eat fruit every day.

Now your turn. Write only the verb:
Write the correct form: My sister ___ (play) tennis on Sundays. (answer with only the verb)
